title: A turn dispatched behind another mints a second session instead of resuming
foundBy: cs-campaign's CI, on the first run with the opencode-fireworks smoke scenario re-enabled
details:
`cs-opencode-remote` and `cs-codex-remote` learn their agent's session id from the first turn's trailing sentinel. Both read it when the process started and stored it after releasing the per-session turn lock. A second turn that overlapped the first therefore read nothing, passed no `--uuid`, and the remote minted a new session.

Turns overlap by design. A campaign dispatches the next turn as soon as the previous turn's reply lands, and the reply is written before the driver that produced it exits.

A new session is not merely untidy under replay. opencode generates a title for a session that has none, which is a model call, and no cassette recorded one at that point. Measured on cs-campaign's CI: an orchestrator ran its two turns on two sessions, the second turn missed the cassette at step 8 of `csrocfw-orchestrator` (`messages: 18 items vs 2`, no tools), and the turn died 11 seconds in. The campaign saw only a member that had gone quiet, waited out its 300s settling window and stalled at 424s.

Sequential turns pass either way, which is why this survived every run on a machine with room.

`cs-claude-remote` does not have it. It mints the session id locally and has nothing to learn.
